dedupe_keys.name: flexibility aware clustering of residential electricity consumption for demand response targeting using high resolution smart meter data

description: Nickie Gkolia, Nikos Dimitropoulos and Vangelis Marinakis publish a Python workflow that segments residential electricity consumption for demand-response targeting. Nine stages prepare PLEGMA household measurements, impute missing values, form fifteen-minute daily profiles, compare DTW and Euclidean clusters, calculate flexibility indicators and test targeting scenarios. The September 2026 Zenodo release archives software under MIT; derived result tables use CC BY 4.0. Original PLEGMA measurements must be obtained separately. The linked results README warns that absolute delta_load values sum interval mean power and require multiplication by 0.25 hours to express watt-hours. Ratio-based results use the original scale consistently, according to the authors. The workflow can supply household flexibility segments for demand-response simulations, but execution and statistical claims were not checked. Geographic and calendar coverage depend on the separately obtained PLEGMA data. A companion Zenodo data release is recorded separately; no related catalogue record explicitly includes this code.
